source.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
source.authors: Catherine Olsson; Nelson Elhage; Neel Nanda; Nicholas Joseph; Nova DasSarma; T. Henighan; Benjamin Mann; Amanda Askell; Yuntao Bai; Anna Chen; Tom Conerly; Dawn Drain; Deep Ganguli; Zac Hatfield-Dodds; Danny Hernandez; Scott Johnston; Andy Jones; John Kernion; Liane Lovitt; Kamal Ndousse; D. record.file_problem: The text is substantially complete, but several figures and the Model Analysis Table are not rendered in the supplied text, so their individual values cannot be extracted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures induction-head behavior and in-context learning during training, alters architecture, and ablates heads to test their relationship.
record.gate_note: The paper reports aggregate training-time and ablation findings in prose. The external replication comments included in the paper are not rows because they report other researchers' results. Individual model-analysis plots and table entries are not separately assignable from the supplied rendering.
record.test_reason: This is an original source. It measures induction-head formation (prefix-matching and copying evaluators), in-context learning score and the loss curve over training in 34 models, shifts formation with a smeared-key architecture, and ablates heads in small models. No verdict labels are given because the study is an original source for the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors claim strong causal evidence that induction heads are the primary ICL mechanism in small attention-only models, only suggestive evidence for small MLP models, and correlational, preliminary evidence that they may explain most ICL in large models. They name simultaneous formation of other composition heads as the main alternative explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses repeated random-sequence copying and prefix-matching measurements, per-token loss-index analysis, architectural perturbation, and pattern-preserving head ablations. The paper also relies on mechanistic analysis from its earlier Transformer Circuits work.
record.method_sensitivity: Changing to the smeared-key architecture allows one-layer models to develop in-context learning and shifts its timing earlier in deeper models. The paper also reports that the observed phase change occurs at different training-token ranges across small and full-scale models.

fits_no_version.finding: After the phase change, the ICL score is roughly constant (~0.4 nats) across model sizes and over the rest of training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size of the in-context learning score after the phase change is invariant to model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: The ordering of loss-curve derivatives across model sizes inverts at the phase change.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling behaviour of the loss derivative switches at the induction-head phase change.

record.problems: Only one training run per model; full-scale models have only 14 or 15 snapshots, limiting temporal resolution; no full-scale ablations; evidence for the majority claim in large models is correlational; individual values in the Model Analysis Table and several plots are not rendered in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The supplied text does not render the individual model-by-model entries from the Model Analysis Table or plotted trajectories, so they cannot be assigned reliably to separate models and conditions. External replication comments and their reported results were excluded because they are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: There are no ablations in full-scale models; the large-model majority claim rests on correlation and analogy. Task-specific few-shot learning is not quantified.
There is one training run per model. The study covers only decoder-only transformers from one lab; other architectures and modalities are not studied.
Only one alternate dataset (books-only) is tried, in small models. Persistence of in-context learning and other data properties are not varied.
Induction heads are not compared with other mechanisms on few-shot task learning.
Fine-grained sub-steps are not analysed. Full-scale models have only 14–15 snapshots.
The study gives no new mechanistic reverse-engineering beyond a summary of prior work, plus validation of the evaluators against the QK eigenvalue trace in small models.

missing.what: Small models trained on a books-only dataset show the phase change developing the same way.
missing.locator: Argument 1, 'Looking at the Phase Change More Closely'; Model Analysis Table

missing.what: In small attention-only models, the prefix-matching evaluator correlates with the previous-token K-composition QK eigenvalue trace, consistent with composition with a previous-token head.
missing.locator: Appendix 'Validating head activation evaluators'; Data Collection (4)

missing.what: Location of induction heads by depth: last layer in attention-only models, second-to-last in 5L/6L MLP models, before mid-depth in 24L/40L models.

Ablating most non-induction heads increases the ICL score. One 6L MLP induction head's ablation has the opposite effect. A non-induction 6L attention-only head's ablation resembles reversing the phase change.
The phase change falls at ~1–3B tokens in small models versus 2.5–5B in the summary; the warm-up schedule overlaps the window (first 1.5e9 tokens).

record.verdict_notes: The study is an original source for V1–V3, so no support/challenge labels are given. The reader's V7 links are wrong: the paper describes a single phase change, and its measures cannot reveal sub-steps. R8–R10 are cherry-picked example heads, not rates. External replications (Redwood, Lieberum) are correctly excluded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures induction-head copying and prefix matching and summarizes a mechanism involving composition with previous-token heads. It does not mechanistically reverse-engineer induction heads across large models with MLPs.
The paper reports a shared training window, but large-model snapshots are sparse and do not establish fine-grained timing within that window.
Ablations bear on the macro loss-index measure in small models; the paper lacks ablations for full-scale models and does not establish that induction heads carry most task-specific few-shot learning.
The paper studies decoder-only Transformers across several model series and sizes, but only one training run per model; it does not test other architectures or modalities.

The paper tests an alternate books-only dataset and a smeared-key architecture. It does not systematically vary all data and training properties or establish persistence of in-context learning across such variations.
The paper distinguishes its general loss-index definition from task-specific few-shot learning but does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot task learning.
The paper reports co-occurrence within a shared window, but does not resolve whether the window contains fine-grained sequential substeps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: 34 decoder-only Transformer language models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Small 1- through 6-layer attention-only and MLP models; full-scale 4-layer, 13M to 40-layer, 13B models; smeared-key models at 1 and 2 layers
rows.stage_stated: Snapshots over training; one training run per model
rows.operation_detail: Measured induction-head prefix matching over training using head activation evaluators.

conditions.value: approximately 2.5 to 5 billion tokens; small models described elsewhere as approximately 1 to 3 billion tokens

rows.measure: Formation of heads scoring as induction heads by prefix matching
rows.baseline: Before the window, induction heads have not yet formed abruptly; one-layer models do not form them.
rows.value: Induction heads form abruptly in the same window as the in-context learning improvement.
rows.locator: Argument 1; Model Analysis Table discussion; Data Collection
rows.note: The paper describes this as a broad pattern across models; specific model-by-model plotted values are unavailable in the supplied rendering.
rows.check: R1 measures when prefix-matching heads form, not composition with a previous-token head, so it should not link to V1. Snapshots resolve only one shared window, not sub-steps, so it cannot show V7's effect. Remove V1 and V7.

source_check.locator_found: Argument 1, lines 370–377; Model Analysis Table, lines 891–909; Model Details, lines 925–926.

rows.subject: 34 decoder-only Transformer language models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Small 1- through 6-layer attention-only and MLP models; full-scale 4-layer, 13M to 40-layer, 13B models; smeared-key models
rows.stage_stated: Snapshots over training; one training run per model
rows.operation_detail: Measured in-context learning as the loss difference between early and later context positions.
rows.measure: In-context learning score; the text gives inconsistent subtraction order in different definitions, but describes the result as the later-token loss advantage
rows.baseline: Before the window, less than 0.15 nats of in-context learning.
rows.value: After the window, roughly 0.4 nats; the paper says this remains roughly constant thereafter.
rows.note: The paper also says more than 75% of final in-context learning forms in this window. The score's subtraction order is inconsistent across the text.
rows.check: The ICL score alone does not attribute in-context learning to induction heads (that is R6's ablation), so drop V3. Drop V7: the measure cannot distinguish sub-steps. The text computes the score both ways (500th minus 50th, and 50th minus 500th); 0.4 nats is the size of the late-token advantage.

source_check.correct: Argument 1 reports less than 0.15 nats before the transition and roughly 0.4 nats afterward, except for the standard one-layer models. Model Details places the small-model transition at approximately 1–3 billion tokens; 2.5–5 billion tokens is not a uniform window for all 34 models. The score supports the ICL component of V2; alone it cannot determine induction-head presence across models for V4.
source_check.locator_found: Key Concepts, lines 159–166; Argument 1, lines 347–358; Model Details, lines 925–926.
source_check.problem: The aggregate condition omits model-specific timing and the one-layer exception; an ICL score alone cannot establish V4's induction-head behaviour.

rows.subject: Transformer language models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Observed the aggregate training loss curve during the induction-head and in-context-learning transition.

conditions.value: same early-training window as the reported phase change

rows.baseline: Loss curve is described as monotonically decreasing in slope outside the transition.
rows.value: A small bump, described as a period of visibly steeper improvement; the paper calls it the only place in training where the loss is not convex.
rows.note: No numerical bump magnitude is stated.
rows.check: The loss bump alone cannot show whether there are sub-steps, so drop V7.

rows.subject: One-layer models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured induction-head scores, in-context learning, and training-loss behavior during training.
rows.measure: Induction-head formation, in-context learning, and phase-change loss bump
rows.baseline: Models with more than one layer show the reported transition.
rows.value: Induction heads never form; in-context learning never substantially develops; the loss bump is absent.
rows.note: The paper attributes the induction-head limitation to the need for composition across attention heads.
rows.check: This is a control. Absence in one-layer models is what V1 predicts, since composition needs two or more layers. It bears on V1 only indirectly, not as a test of mechanism. Linking it to V4 is questionable, because it shows non-universality at depth one; keep V4 only if the version's scope excludes one-layer models.

rows.subject: Smeared-key models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Trained models with keys interpolated between the current token's key and the previous token's key using a trainable parameter.

conditions.value: one layer and two or more layers

rows.measure: Development and timing of in-context learning
rows.baseline: Without smeared keys, the one-layer models do not develop the reported in-context learning transition; deeper models develop it later.
rows.value: In-context learning forms in one-layer models and forms earlier in two-layer and larger models.
rows.note: The paper says induction-head formation shifts along with in-context learning, but the specific per-model values are in unavailable plots/table entries.
rows.check: This is an architecture change, not a data change. It bears on V5 only if V5's 'training setup' includes architecture. The paper shows smeared-key models only at 1 and 2 layers ('We present these only at one-layer and two-layer sizes'), so 'two-layer and larger' overstates the scope.

source_check.correct: The presented smeared-key models have one or two layers only. Argument 2 describes ICL developing in one-layer models and earlier development in two-layer and larger models, but Model Details restricts the presented experiment to one- and two-layer sizes.
source_check.locator_found: Argument 2, lines 519–545; Model Details, Smeared Key Models, lines 1008–1021.
source_check.problem: The condition extends the presented experiment beyond its documented one- and two-layer models.

rows.subject: Small attention-only models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Pattern-preserving ablated individual attention heads, including induction heads, by zeroing their residual-stream contribution while preserving attention patterns.
rows.baseline: Unablated model's in-context learning score; numerical value not stated.
rows.value: Ablating induction heads greatly decreases in-context learning; the authors say almost all in-context learning in small attention-only models appears to come from these heads.
rows.note: The paper states this holds from the start of the phase change through the end of training. Numerical per-head results are not rendered in the supplied text.
rows.check: This holds only for small attention-only models. V3's large-model claim has no ablation; there are no full-scale ablations.

rows.subject: Small models with MLPs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Ablated individual attention heads and measured the change in in-context learning.
rows.baseline: Unablated model; numerical value not stated.
rows.value: The paper includes MLP-model ablations in its evidence, but characterizes the conclusion about induction heads as only suggestive in the MLP case.
rows.note: The supplied text does not give aggregate numerical ablation effects for this model family.
rows.check: The authors rate 'contributes majority' as medium/suggestive for MLP models. One 6L MLP induction head has the opposite effect on the score.

source_check.correct: The authors rate evidence for a majority contribution in small MLP models as medium/causal and describe the conclusion as suggestive. This does not establish an incomplete majority effect. For the majority claim, use cannot_determine rather than partial. A six-layer MLP model also has an induction head whose ablation changes the score in the opposite direction.
source_check.locator_found: Summary of Evidence, lines 279–295; Argument 3, lines 550–593; Additional Curiosities, lines 1074–1078.
source_check.problem: The partial state converts uncertainty about a majority contribution into evidence of an incomplete effect.

rows.subject: 40-layer model, 13 billion parameters; literal copying head
rows.operation_detail: Measured the head's copying and prefix-matching scores and inspected its repeated-text behavior.
rows.measure: Copying score and prefix-matching score; literal sequence repetition behavior
rows.value: Copying score 0.89; prefix-matching score 0.75; the head is described as predicting repeated names, phrases, and sentences by attending to earlier instances.
rows.locator: Argument 4, table of example heads; Behavior 1
rows.note: The paper defines induction heads by both sequence-copying and prefix-matching behavior.
rows.check: This is a 13B model with MLPs, outside V1's 'small attention-only' scope, so remove V1. The values are selected example heads, not systematic rates.

source_check.locator_found: Argument 4, example-head table and Behavior 1, lines 623–673.

rows.subject: 40-layer model, 13 billion parameters; translation head
rows.operation_detail: Measured the head's copying and prefix-matching scores and inspected English, French, and German translation behavior.
rows.measure: Copying and prefix-matching scores; contribution to translation
rows.value: Copying score 0.20; prefix-matching score 0.85; direct logit attributions show clear net contribution to correct translation, though they are not always direct or sharp.
rows.locator: Argument 4, table of example heads; Behavior 2
rows.note: The translation contribution is explicitly qualified as imperfect and sometimes requiring later-layer processing.
rows.check: For V4 the head meets the induction definition (prefix matching 0.85), so the state is observed. The 'partial' state concerns translation, which no version names. Remove V1. This is a selected example.

rows.subject: 40-layer model, 13 billion parameters; pattern-matching head
rows.operation_detail: Measured induction-head scores and attention allocation on synthetic category-pattern examples.

conditions.value: 8 / 40 in the summary table; 26 / 40 in the prose

rows.measure: Copying score, prefix-matching score, and attention allocated to correct category positions
rows.value: Copying score 0.69; prefix-matching score 0.94; about 65% of attention from colons goes to correct positions.
rows.locator: Argument 4, table of example heads; Behavior 3
rows.note: The head layer is inconsistent between the summary table and prose. The paper says the behavior is not perfect.
rows.check: Remove V1. The head's layer is inconsistent: 8/40 in the table and 26/40 in the prose. The 65% attention figure concerns abstract pattern matching, not a version. This is a selected example.

relation.reason: Its own training measurements, architectural interventions and small-model ablations directly investigate induction-head formation and its connection to ICL.

tranche.reason: This original study establishes the induction-head, token-index loss, architectural-intervention and ablation measurements used as the baseline.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased. Large-model majority attribution remains indirect; no full-scale ablations are reported. The text inconsistently reverses the ICL score's subtraction order, and graphical per-head ablation values are unavailable.
